summary:
West Java stands under the national framework of Indonesia; the findings below are those specific to the province.

On 22 June 2025 the West Java Regional Police detained 75 people at a privately rented villa in the Puncak area of Bogor Regency, acting on a tip from local residents. Police described the gathering as an LGBT "family gathering" held "to avoid detection".

Amnesty International condemned the arrests on 24 June 2025 as a discriminatory raid and "a blatant violation of human rights and privacy", stated that the gathering violated no law, and demanded the release of those held and accountability for the operation.

In August 2026 men doused a trans woman with what appeared to be urine on a street in Bogor, one of a wave of attacks on trans women in the province.

Activists link that violence to a 2025 presidential regulation classifying the spread of LGBTQ culture as a non-military threat and to discriminatory regional regulations, arguing that official language of this kind legitimises violence against trans women.

A trans woman quoted in the reporting said that people who previously appeared in public now live in fear.
tangentialFactors:
Two channels of risk are documented in the province: street violence carried out by private individuals, and police enforcement against LGBTI gatherings. A visitor who avoids one does not thereby avoid the other.

The June 2025 operation targeted a privately rented villa rather than a licensed venue, so holding a gathering on private property did not shield it from police action.
localsOnly:
For trans residents, visibility in public space is the immediate exposure. The trans woman quoted in the August 2026 reporting described a shift in which people who previously appeared in public now live in fear.

Police action in the province has followed residents' reports: the Puncak raid came after a tip from local residents, which makes neighbour reporting a practical route by which gatherings and individuals come to police attention.

Activists point to discriminatory regional regulations in force in the province as part of the environment that sustains violence against trans women.
outOfScopeNotes:
The charges brought against the 75 people detained in Puncak, and whether they were released, are not established in the sources reviewed.

The specific regional regulations that activists describe as discriminatory are not identified by name or content in the material available.

No prosecution statistics for West Java, and no information on whether the August 2026 attack in Bogor was investigated, were found.
